PUBLIC DATA PILOT

Federal procurement

Historical COVID-19 response
Quantities as of August 31, 2022
Research collected November 19, 2026
Coverage matters. This pilot covers seven medical categories from a federal emergency purchasing report. It is not a current national top ten, annual hospital usage, or a census of Canadian healthcare purchases. Unit prices and complete manufacturing-country shares are not published in this snapshot.

Quantity purchased

Count comparable units: a mask, a pair of gloves or a litre of sanitizer. Orders and deliveries are shown separately; neither tells us how much was used in patient care.

Cost per item

Actual item prices need item-level quantities and net spending. A contract’s total value can include services, accessories or factory setup, so dividing it by units is not always a product price.

Where it is made

A Canadian supplier may sell imported products. We show manufacturing evidence separately from supplier location, with missing information clearly identified.

How to prepare the records

Required columns: row_id, product_id, item, buyer, fiscal_year, unit, quantity, net_cost_cad, manufacturing_country, source. Use one row per purchase line and manufacturing country. Split a line only when the quantities and costs by origin are documented. Row IDs must be unique. Group equivalent products under one product ID; use a different ID for different models or specifications.

Convert packs and boxes into each, pair or litre before uploading. Quantity must be positive. Net cost must be nonnegative CAD, consistently excluding tax and separately priced service contracts; leave it blank if unknown. Use Canada for Canadian manufacture, the actual country name for foreign manufacture, and a blank or Unknown when unverified. The source column must contain an https:// or http:// evidence link. Do not infer origin from the vendor’s address.

All quantity rows contribute to the quantity list. A product enters the cost-per-item list only when every purchase line has a cost. Unit cost is quantity-weighted: net spending divided by units. An incomplete product has no spending-based origin breakdown. These lists describe your uploaded records only; they do not establish national coverage.

SOURCES & METHODS

Evidence you can check.

The public pilot preserves the dates and scope of each source. We have not used import values as a substitute for what hospitals bought, or filled missing prices with estimates.

Download evidence and source metadataDownload collection notes
What is included in the quantity list?

Seven medical categories in PSPC’s cumulative federal COVID-19 report as of August 31, 2022. Two nonmedical mask categories are excluded. Products are ranked only within the same reported unit. There are five categories measured as individual items, one in pairs and one in litres. We show fewer than ten rather than add unsupported entries. Mask orders include long-term contracts.

PSPC quantity table
Can manufacturing percentages be combined with these quantities?

No. PHAC’s June 23, 2022 note reports approximately 70% domestic production for N95 respirators, 50% for surgical masks, 100% for face shields and 25% for disposable gowns. These are a separate historical procurement statement. We do not multiply them by the August quantities. The gown categories do not match, and no share is assigned to the broader gown total. Foreign manufacturing countries and the underlying shares by spending are not disclosed in that note.

PHAC manufacturing statement
Why are there no national price rankings?

The collected public sources do not supply a complete, comparable item-level dataset of Canadian healthcare purchases, quantities, net prices and manufacturing origin. CanadaBuys covers federal contracting; CIHI provides health-system financial and operational context. Neither source, as reviewed here, establishes the requested nationwide item rankings.
